original.title: Chicken Katsu Curry
original.description: Crispy panko-crusted chicken cutlets served over rice with a mild, sweet-savory Japanese curry sauce full of carrots and potatoes.
ingredients: 2 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into chunks
1 (3.5 oz) box Japanese curry roux (such as Golden Curry), broken into pieces
4 (5 oz) boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts, pounded to 1/2 inch thick
4 cups cooked Japanese short-grain rice, for serving
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the onion, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the carrots and potatoes, stir for 1 minute, then pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, skim any foam, and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Turn off the heat, add the curry roux pieces, and stir until completely dissolved.
Stir in the ketchup and honey, then simmer over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens; keep warm.
Season the chicken on both sides with salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes with the flour, beaten eggs, and panko, then coat each cutlet in flour, dip in egg, and press firmly into the panko.
Heat the frying oil in a deep skillet to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the cutlets two at a time for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Drain the katsu on a wire rack for 3 minutes, then slice into strips.
Spoon rice onto plates, lay the sliced katsu alongside, and ladle the curry sauce over and around it.

original.title: Oyakodon (Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
original.description: A comforting donburi of chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy-dashi broth, finished with softly set egg over rice.
ingredients: 8 oz boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
steps: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small skillet and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the onion slices and simmer for 3 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the chicken in a single layer and simmer for 6 to 7 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Lightly beat the eggs in a bowl, leaving some streaks of white and yolk.
Pour about two thirds of the egg evenly over the chicken, cover, and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the remaining egg, cover again, and turn off the heat; let stand 30 seconds so the egg stays soft and silky.
Divide the hot rice between two bowls and slide the chicken and egg mixture with some of the broth over the top.
Garnish with green onion and a pinch of shichimi togarashi and serve immediately.

original.title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelet)
original.description: A lightly sweet, layered rolled omelet that is a staple of Japanese breakfasts and bento boxes.
steps: Whisk the eggs, dashi, sugar, mirin, soy sauce, and salt in a bowl until well combined but not foamy.
Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan or 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and wipe it with a little oil using a folded paper towel.
Pour in about a quarter of the egg mixture and tilt the pan to coat the bottom in a thin layer.
When the egg is just set on the bottom but still slightly wet on top, roll it from the far side toward you into a log.
Push the roll back to the far side of the pan and wipe the empty part of the pan with oil again.
Pour in another quarter of the egg, lifting the roll so the raw egg flows underneath it.
When the new layer is nearly set, roll the log back toward you, wrapping it in the new layer.
Repeat with the remaining egg mixture to build up the layers.
Transfer the omelet to a bamboo mat or plastic wrap, shape it into a neat rectangle, and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Slice into 1-inch pieces and serve warm or at room temperature.

original.title: Chicken Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
original.description: Juicy bite-size chicken thighs marinated in soy, ginger, and garlic, then coated in potato starch and fried until extra crisp.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
steps: Place the chicken in a bowl with the soy sauce, sake, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, and sugar and toss well.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Drain off any excess marinade and toss the chicken pieces in the potato starch until evenly coated, shaking off the excess.
Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until pale golden, then transfer to a wire rack and rest for 4 minutes.
Raise the oil temperature to 350°F (180°C).
Fry the chicken a second time for 1 to 2 minutes until deep golden and very crisp.
Drain on the rack and serve hot with lemon wedges and mayonnaise.

original.title: Yakisoba (Stir-Fried Noodles)
original.description: Chewy wheat noodles stir-fried with pork, cabbage, and carrots in a tangy-sweet yakisoba sauce, a favorite at Japanese festivals.
ingredients: 3 (5 oz) packages fresh yakisoba or chukamen noodles
6 oz thinly sliced pork belly or pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tbsp aonori (dried green seaweed), for garnish
2 tbsp pickled red ginger (beni shoga), for garnish
steps: Whisk the Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, and sugar together in a small bowl.
Rinse the noodles briefly under hot water to loosen them, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 3 minutes until browned.
Add the onion and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Add the noodles and green onions and toss for 2 minutes until heated through.
Pour the sauce over the noodles and toss continuously for 1 to 2 minutes until evenly coated.
Serve topped with aonori and pickled red ginger.

original.title: Chawanmushi (Savory Steamed Egg Custard)
original.description: A silky, delicate egg custard steamed in cups with dashi, shrimp, chicken, and mushrooms.
ingredients: 2 oz boneless chicken thigh, cut into small pieces
4 sprigs mitsuba or 1 green onion, chopped
steps: Gently whisk the eggs in a bowl without creating foam, then stir in the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and salt.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a measuring cup to make it perfectly smooth.
Divide the shrimp, chicken, and mushrooms among four heatproof cups or ramekins.
Pour the egg mixture into the cups and skim off any bubbles from the surface.
Cover each cup with foil or a lid.
Bring water to a boil in a steamer, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Steam the cups over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the custard is set but still jiggles slightly in the center.
Top with mitsuba or green onion and serve hot.

original.title: Matcha Latte
original.description: Bright green tea whisked to a froth and poured over steamed milk with a touch of sweetness.
ingredients: 1 to 2 tsp honey or sugar, to taste
steps: Sift the matcha into a wide mug or bowl to remove any lumps.
Add the hot water and whisk vigorously in a zigzag motion with a bamboo whisk or small frother for 30 seconds until frothy.
Heat the milk in a small saucepan over medium heat until steaming, about 3 minutes, without letting it boil.
Froth the milk with a frother or whisk until foamy.
Stir the honey or sugar into the matcha, then pour in the frothed milk and serve immediately.

original.title: Chicken Teriyaki
original.description: Pan-seared chicken thighs with crisp skin glazed in a glossy homemade soy, mirin, and sake sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season lightly with salt.
Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and place the chicken skin side down.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes without moving, pressing gently, until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more until it reaches 165°F (74°C) inside.
Wipe out the excess fat with a paper towel and pour the sauce into the pan.
Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning the sauce over the chicken, until it reduces to a sticky glaze.
Slice the chicken, drizzle with the remaining glaze, and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onion.

original.title: Yakitori (Grilled Chicken Skewers)
original.description: Bite-size chicken thigh and green onion skewers grilled over high heat and brushed with sweet-savory tare sauce.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
6 green onions (white and light green parts), cut into 1-inch lengths
12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
steps: Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, and green onion tops in a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until reduced by about a third and slightly syrupy, then discard the onion tops.
Thread the chicken and green onion pieces alternately onto the soaked skewers.
Preheat a grill or broiler to high, about 450°F (230°C), and brush the grates or pan with oil.
Grill the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side until lightly charred.
Brush the skewers generously with tare and grill for 1 minute more per side, repeating two or three times to build a glaze.
Check that the chicken is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Serve hot with extra tare and a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi.

original.title: Sunomono (Japanese Cucumber Salad)
original.description: A crisp, refreshing salad of paper-thin cucumbers and wakame in a light sweet rice vinegar dressing.
steps: Slice the cucumbers as thinly as possible into rounds.
Toss the cucumbers with the salt in a bowl and let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, soak the wakame in cold water for 5 to 10 minutes until rehydrated, then drain and squeeze dry.
Squeeze the cucumbers firmly to remove the excess liquid.
Stir together the rice vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce until the sugar dissolves.
Combine the cucumbers and wakame with the dressing and toss well.
Chill for at least 10 minutes and serve sprinkled with sesame seeds.

original.title: Spinach Gomaae (Spinach with Sesame Dressing)
original.description: Blanched spinach tossed in a nutty, slightly sweet toasted sesame dressing, a classic Japanese side dish.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and prepare a bowl of ice water.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking often, until fragrant and golden.
Grind the warm seeds in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder until about half are crushed.
Mix the ground sesame with the soy sauce, sugar, and mirin to form a thick dressing.
Blanch the spinach for 30 to 45 seconds, then transfer immediately to the ice water.
Drain the spinach, gather it into a bundle, and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Cut the spinach into 1 1/2-inch lengths and toss with the sesame dressing just before serving.

original.title: Zaru Soba (Cold Buckwheat Noodles)
original.description: Chilled buckwheat noodles served on a bamboo tray with a savory dipping sauce, a cooling summer favorite.
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
steps: Combine the dashi, soy sauce, and mirin in a small saucepan and bring to a simmer for 1 minute.
Cool the dipping sauce, then chill it in the refrigerator.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the soba noodles, stirring to separate them.
Cook the noodles according to the package, usually 4 to 5 minutes, until just tender.
Drain and rinse the noodles thoroughly under cold running water, rubbing gently to remove the surface starch.
Plunge the noodles into ice water for 1 minute, then drain well.
Arrange the noodles on bamboo trays or plates and top with nori strips.
Serve with small cups of the chilled dipping sauce, green onions, and wasabi to stir in to taste.

original.title: Kitsune Udon
original.description: Thick udon noodles in a light dashi broth topped with sweet simmered fried tofu pouches.
steps: Pour boiling water over the aburaage to remove excess oil, then drain and squeeze gently.
Simmer the aburaage with 1/2 cup dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan over low heat for 10 minutes, turning once, until most of the liquid is absorbed.
In a separate pot, bring the 3 cups dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt to a simmer.
Cook the udon in a large pot of boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes until heated through and loosened, then drain.
Divide the noodles between two large bowls and ladle the hot broth over them.
Top each bowl with two pieces of simmered aburaage, kamaboko if using, and green onions.
Serve immediately.

original.title: Miso-Glazed Cod
original.description: Cod fillets marinated in a sweet white miso mixture and broiled until caramelized and flaky.
ingredients: 4 (6 oz) cod or black cod fillets, skin on
steps: Whisk the miso, mirin, sake, and sugar together until smooth.
Pat the fish dry and coat it all over with the miso mixture in a shallow dish.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 2 days.
Preheat the broiler with the rack about 6 inches from the heat and line a baking sheet with lightly oiled foil.
Wipe most of the marinade off the fish, leaving a thin film, and place the fillets skin side down on the sheet.
Broil for 8 to 12 minutes until the surface is deeply caramelized in spots and the fish flakes easily.
Garnish with green onion and serve with steamed rice.

original.title: Shokupan (Japanese Milk Bread)
original.description: A tall, fluffy, slightly sweet white sandwich loaf made extra soft with a cooked flour paste called tangzhong.
steps: Whisk the 3 tbsp flour and 1/2 cup milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until it thickens to a paste, then let it cool.
Combine the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt in a stand mixer bowl.
Add the warm milk, egg, and cooled tangzhong and knead with the dough hook on low for 5 minutes.
Add the softened butter and knead on medium for 10 to 12 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled.
Punch down the dough, divide it into 3 equal pieces, and roll each into an oval, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Place the rolls seam side down in a greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan, cover, and let rise for 45 to 60 minutes until the dough reaches the rim.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Brush the top with milk and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 190°F (88°C).
Turn out onto a rack and cool completely before slicing.

original.title: Dorayaki (Red Bean Pancakes)
original.description: Two fluffy honey pancakes sandwiched around sweet red bean paste, a beloved Japanese snack.
steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar, and honey in a bowl for 2 minutes until pale and slightly fluffy.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and stir just until smooth.
Cover and let the batter rest for 15 minutes, then stir in water a tablespoon at a time until it flows like thick pancake batter.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and wipe it with a little oil, removing the excess with a paper towel.
Pour about 3 tbsp batter into the pan to form a 3 1/2-inch round.
Cook for about 1 1/2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface, then flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Transfer the pancakes to a plate and cover with a damp towel to keep them soft.
Spread about 3 tbsp red bean paste on one pancake, top with a second, and press the edges gently to seal.

original.title: Japanese Souffle Cheesecake
original.description: A light, jiggly cotton-soft cheesecake that is baked gently in a water bath.
steps: Preheat the oven to 320°F (160°C) and line the bottom and sides of an 8-inch round cake pan (not springform) with parchment that extends 2 inches above the rim.
Melt the cream cheese, butter, and milk together in a bowl set over simmering water, whisking until smooth, then let cool slightly.
Whisk in the egg yolks one at a time, then sift in the cake flour and cornstarch and whisk until smooth; stir in the lemon juice.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar until foamy, then gradually add the sugar and beat to soft-to-medium peaks.
Fold one third of the whites into the yolk mixture to lighten it, then gently fold in the rest until no streaks remain.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and tap it on the counter to release large bubbles.
Set the pan in a larger roasting pan and pour in hot water to come 1 inch up the sides.
Bake for 25 minutes, then reduce the oven to 285°F (140°C) and bake for 45 to 55 minutes more until golden and set.
Turn off the oven and leave the cake inside with the door slightly open for 15 minutes to prevent collapsing.
Remove from the pan, cool, and dust with powdered sugar before serving warm or chilled.

original.title: Hambagu (Japanese Hamburger Steak)
original.description: Tender beef and pork patties pan-seared and simmered in a glossy ketchup and Worcestershire pan sauce, a home-style yoshoku classic.
steps: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 to 8 minutes until soft and golden, then cool completely.
Soak the panko in the milk for 5 minutes.
Combine the beef, pork, egg, soaked panko, cooled onion, salt, pepper, and nutmeg and knead by hand for 1 to 2 minutes until sticky.
Divide into 4 portions, toss each between your hands to remove air pockets, and shape into 3/4-inch-thick ovals with a slight dent in the center.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the patties for 3 minutes until browned.
Flip, add 2 tbsp water, cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Transfer the patties to plates and add the wine, ketchup, and Worcestershire sauce to the pan.
Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, then swirl in the butter.
Spoon the sauce over the patties and serve with rice and a green salad.

original.title: Japanese Potato Salad
original.description: Creamy mashed-and-chunky potato salad with cucumber, carrot, egg, and ham dressed in tangy Japanese mayonnaise.
ingredients: 2 lb russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1/2 small carrot, thinly sliced into quarter moons
steps: Place the potatoes in a pot of cold salted water, bring to a boil, and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until tender.
Add the carrot slices for the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Drain well, return the potatoes to the hot pot, and shake over low heat for 1 minute to dry them.
Roughly mash the potatoes, leaving some chunks, and stir in the rice vinegar while still hot; let cool to room temperature.
Toss the cucumber and onion with a pinch of salt, let stand for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Fold the cucumber, onion, carrot, eggs, and ham into the potatoes.
Stir in the mayonnaise, season with salt and pepper, and chill for 30 minutes before serving.
